content.title: About
content.content: The white hot‑dog roll is a soft, slightly sweet wheat‑flour bun designed for serving sausages, frankfurters and a variety of toppings. It has a small cylindrical shape, about 12 cm long, making it easy to hold in the hand.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: These buns are a staple of street food in the United States and Canada.
The dough usually contains a modest amount of sugar and butter, giving it a more tender crumb than regular bread.
Some recipes add milk or egg yolk to achieve a golden crust.
Buns are often served warm, which keeps them soft and aromatic.
In Russia a similar product is sold as “sausage buns,” often frozen for convenience.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Provides a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains modest protein
items.content: Wheat flour contributes a small amount of plant‑based protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Enriched flour can supply B1, B2 and niacin, which support metabolism.

items.title: Versatile pairing
items.content: Neutral flavor allows the bun to complement a wide range of fillings, vegetables, proteins and sauces.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of carbs and a little fat makes the bun satisfying, helping to curb hunger.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Contains wheat flour, so it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar, which may be problematic for diabetics.

items.title: Salt and sugar content
items.content: Some commercial recipes add salt and sugar, which should be considered in restricted diets.

items.title: Preservatives in industrial versions
items.content: Frozen or pre‑packaged buns may contain additives that not everyone tolerates well.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Warm the bun in an oven or microwave for 30–60 seconds, split it lengthwise and place a sausage, frankfurter, vegetables, cheese, sauces or any favorite toppings. Common additions include mustard, ketchup, mayo and fresh veggies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen buns in a freezer at –18 °C. After thawing, store in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Fresh buns stored in the refrigerator stay good for 5–7 days.
